scope: Claim-level evidence for the remaining unmapped Part 10 canopy-adjustment, wound-recovery, spacing, canopy-depth, canopy-geometry, and measurement lessons.
rules: Direct cannabis evidence is used for architecture, canopy-position, density, and treatment-response claims only within studied contexts.
General wound biology, measurement policy, and metadata standards support method and interpretation, not cannabis-specific performance thresholds.
Evidence mappings remain review-pending and do not authorize publication, visual approval, or assessment approval.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Repositioning foliage can change local shading while preserving leaf area, but peer-reviewed cannabis literature supports broader architecture/light-position effects rather than a universal leaf-tucking schedule or guaranteed yield benefit.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Danziger and Bernstein 2021 architecture-modulation study; Danziger and Bernstein 2021 Plants 10(9):1834 abstract/results on architecture, light penetration, and within-plant spatial variation.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports treating leaf tucking as a reversible canopy adjustment whose effect should be measured rather than assumed.
claimEvidence.limitations: Neither source is a controlled leaf-tucking trial, so no timing, frequency, or yield rule is established.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: High-stress stem manipulation combines structural injury with later regeneration and branch-control responses; recovery should be assessed as wound repair and resumed function, not inferred from visible swelling alone.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Omary et al. 2023 review of systemic plant regeneration and wound repair; Danziger and Bernstein 2021 architecture-treatment context; Ijoma et al. 2026 review of high-stress cannabis training and research gaps.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports conservative supercropping recovery monitoring and separation of wound healing from production claims.
claimEvidence.limitations: Direct standardized cannabis supercropping trials remain limited; no universal injury severity or recovery interval is established.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis planting density changes yield per plant, yield per area, lower-canopy conditions, and chemical uniformity, so spacing decisions require area-based as well as plant-based measurements.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Danziger and Bernstein 2022 abstract/results/conclusions on 1 versus 2 plants per square meter and density-by-architecture effects; Shape Matters 2021 canopy-position and light-gradient findings.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports measuring spacing, canopy closure, internal conditions, and both per-plant and per-area yield.
claimEvidence.limitations: The tested densities, cultivar, and greenhouse conditions are not universal spacing targets.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Large and/or dense cannabis canopies can develop strong vertical light gradients associated with lower-canopy changes in morphology and cannabinoid concentration, supporting multi-depth light mapping rather than reliance on a top-canopy reading.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Shape Matters 2021 abstract/results on light penetration and cannabinoid gradients in large plants; Danziger and Bernstein 2022 abstract/results on chronic lower-canopy light deprivation under higher density.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports vertical PPFD profiles and mapped canopy-depth interpretation.
claimEvidence.limitations: The studies do not establish one universal productive canopy depth or fixed lower-canopy PPFD cutoff.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis architecture changes within-canopy light distribution and chemical uniformity, but available studies do not establish that one horizontal or vertical canopy geometry is universally superior across lighting layouts, densities, cultivars, and production objectives.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Shape Matters 2021 architecture/light-position results and conclusions; Danziger and Bernstein 2022 density-by-architecture interaction results.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports matching canopy geometry to lighting geometry and normalizing outcomes by clearly defined system denominators.
claimEvidence.limitations: Neither study is a standardized horizontal-versus-vertical production-system trial.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Canopy comparisons require repeatable locations, defined measurands and units, controlled measurement context, and clear normalization because yield per plant, yield per area, canopy position, and photon environment answer different questions.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: NIST metrological-traceability policy for measurand/traceability/uncertainty; MIAPPE v1.2 metadata structure for treatments, environments, biological material, and observations; Danziger and Bernstein 2022 and Shape Matters 2021 for cannabis plant-versus-area and spatial canopy outcomes.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's grid-based canopy records, light maps, intervention logs, harvest-zone identity, and denominator discipline.
claimEvidence.limitations: NIST and MIAPPE structure measurement evidence but do not establish cannabis performance targets; cannabis studies remain system-specific.
